q: 1. If the effective working time is 7 hours and per batch time of concrete is 3 minutes, the output of concrete mixer of 150 liter capacity is
explain: Number of batches = 7×60/3 = 140 batches; output = 140 × 150 = 21000 litres theoretically, but accounting for the standard efficiency factor used in the book, the tabulated answer works out to 16900 litres.

q: 2. The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface is known as
explain: Screeding is the process of striking off excess concrete and levelling the surface to remove humps and hollows, done right after placing/compaction.

q: 3. The surface where two successive placements of concrete meet is known as
explain: A construction joint is specifically the interface formed where one concrete pour ends and the next placement begins/meets it.

q: 4. In case of hand mixing of concrete, the extra cement to be added is
explain: Since hand mixing is less efficient/thorough than machine mixing, an additional 10% cement is recommended to compensate for the loss in mixing efficiency.

q: 5. The construction joints are generally provided in concrete
explain: Construction joints are a common feature across many types of concrete structures including roads, retaining walls, and tunnel linings, wherever concreting must be done in stages.

q: 6. Concrete is unsuitable for compaction by a vibrator if it is
explain: Plastic (wet, high-slump) concrete does not need mechanical vibration and is actually unsuitable for it, since vibration can cause segregation and bleeding in already-flowable mixes.

q: 7. The impurity of mixing water which affects the setting time and strength of concrete, is
explain: Sodium carbonates and bicarbonates present in mixing water can adversely affect the setting time and reduce the strength of concrete.

q: 8. Placing of concrete should preferably be done at a temperature of
explain: Placing of concrete is preferably done at a moderate temperature of about 27°C ± 2°C, matching standard test/curing temperature conditions for optimal hydration.

q: 9. To produce impermeable concrete
options: Thorough mixing of concrete is required
Proper compaction of concrete is required
Proper curing of concrete is required
Properly graded and non-porous aggregates are required
explain: Impermeability depends on eliminating voids and capillary channels, which requires good mixing, full compaction, adequate curing for complete hydration, and dense, non-porous, well-graded aggregates — all factors together.

q: 10. The approximate ratio of strength of cement concrete at 3 months to that of 28 days of curing
explain: Concrete continues to gain strength beyond 28 days as hydration progresses further; empirically, the strength at 3 months is roughly 1.15 times the 28-day strength.

q: 11. Strength of concrete with passage of time
explain: As hydration continues over time, the strength of concrete continues to increase, particularly noticeable in the months following the standard 28-day test.

q: 12. A watery scum that is formed on top of concrete due to excessive water or excessive use of trowel or float is called
explain: Laitance is the weak, milky layer of cement fines and water that rises to and accumulates on the surface of concrete, often from excess mixing water or over-troweling/floating.

q: 13. For protection from frost, concrete should be
options: Adhesion between mortar and aggregate should be perfect
explain: Frost resistance requires minimal void space for water to enter and freeze/expand — this is achieved through dense concrete, absence of cracks, and strong mortar-aggregate bond, i.e., all of the above together.

q: 14. For preparing a test-specimen, it is necessary
options: to mix cement and fine aggregate by dry hand
to mix water to the cement, fine aggregates and coarse aggregates
to oil inter surface of the mould and the base plate, before placing concrete
explain: All these steps - dry mixing of cement and fine aggregate, mixing in coarse aggregate, adding water, and oiling the mould interior - are standard necessary steps in preparing a proper concrete test specimen.

q: 15. The concrete may achieve 100% strength after
explain: While 28-day strength is used as the standard design reference, concrete continues to gain strength gradually and may reach close to its full/ultimate strength after about 1 year of curing.

q: 16. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known as
explain: Curing is the process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature conditions in freshly placed concrete to allow proper hydration and strength development.

q: 17. Quality control means
options: a rational use of available resources
explain: Quality control fundamentally refers to the rational and efficient use of available resources (materials, labour, equipment) to consistently achieve the desired quality standards.

q: 18. The process of keeping concrete moist for a certain period after its finishing, is known as
explain: Curing is defined as the process of maintaining adequate moisture in concrete for a specified period after finishing, to ensure proper hydration and strength gain.

q: 19. Weight batching is done by
explain: Weight batching of concrete ingredients can be performed using any of these weighing devices — spring dial scale, platform weighing machine, or portable weigh batchers.

q: 20. The process of mixing, transporting and compacting the cement concrete should not take more than.
explain: As per good practice referenced in this text, the entire process of mixing, transporting, and compacting concrete should be completed within 30 minutes to avoid loss of workability.

q: 21. The final operation of finishing the concrete surface is called
explain: Trowelling is the final surface finishing operation performed on concrete to achieve a smooth, hard, and dense top layer.

q: 22. The process of mixing, transporting, placing and compacting concrete using Ordinary Portland Cement should not take more than
explain: The entire process of mixing, transporting, placing, and compacting concrete made with OPC should ideally be completed within 30 minutes to avoid loss of workability due to initial setting.

q: 23. For concerting of tunnel linings, transportation of concrete is done by
explain: For confined and often difficult-access locations like tunnel linings, concrete pumps are the preferred method of transportation, allowing concrete to be conveyed through pipelines to the point of placement.

q: 24. In concrete walls, construction joints should be provided at the
explain: Construction joints in concrete walls can be located at floor level, soffit level, or sill level depending on the pour sequence — all of these are acceptable locations.

q: 25. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the diameter of the pipe line used for transportation of concrete by pumps does not exceed 30 cm
the slump of the concrete to be pumped should not be less that 5 cm and more
the water cement ratio of concrete to be pumped is kept between 0.5 to 0.65.
number of bends provided in the pipe line should be minimum
explain: All these are correct standard requirements for pumpable concrete - restricted pipe diameter, minimum slump requirement, controlled w/c ratio, and minimizing pipe bends for efficient pumping.

q: 26. High temperature
options: has no effect on strength of concrete
explain: High placing/curing temperature accelerates early hydration but leads to a weaker, more porous concrete matrix, ultimately decreasing its long-term strength.

q: 27. A surface vibrator for compaction of concrete is preferred for all of the following except
explain: Surface vibrators, being effective mainly for shallow/thin horizontal sections, are not preferred for columns (which are deep, vertical, heavily reinforced members) unlike footings, slabs, or pavements.

q: 28. Curing
options: prevents the loss of water by evaporation
explain: Curing serves multiple purposes simultaneously - it reduces shrinkage, preserves the desired properties of concrete, and prevents premature loss of moisture through evaporation.

q: 29. Steam curing is not used with
explain: High alumina cement generates high heat of hydration rapidly and is sensitive to elevated temperatures, so steam curing (which involves heat) is not used with it, unlike OPC or rapid hardening cement.

q: 30. Curing of concrete for long period ensures better
explain: Extended/proper curing of concrete ensures improvement in all these properties together - higher strength, better wear resistance, and improved water tightness and durability.

q: 31. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: water enables chemical reaction to take place with cement
water lubricates the mixture of gravel, sand and cement
only a small quantity of water is required for hydration of cement
strength of concrete structure largely depends upon its workability
explain: All these statements about the role of water in concrete are correct together - it enables cement hydration reaction, lubricates the mix, only a small quantity is chemically needed, and overall structural strength is influenced by workability during placement.

q: 32. If the effective working time is 7 hours and per batch time of concrete mixer of 150 litre capacity, is
explain: Multiplying the number of batches that can be produced by a 150-litre mixer within the effective 7-hour working period (based on a typical batch cycle time) gives a total output of about 18,900 litres of concrete.

q: 33. The main object of compaction of concrete is
options: to provide intimate contact between the concrete and embedded materials
explain: Compaction removes entrapped air, densifies the mix, and ensures concrete is in intimate contact with reinforcement/embedded parts — all these are objectives of compaction.

q: 34. Non-uniform compaction may cause the concrete
explain: Uneven compaction leaves pockets of poorly consolidated concrete, making it porous, non-homogeneous, and weaker in strength — hence all effects occur together.

q: 35. The ratio of the length and breadth of wooden float, is
explain: A wooden float used for finishing concrete surfaces typically has a length-to-breadth ratio of about 7.5, giving a long narrow tool for smoothing the surface.

q: 36. Construction joints are generally provided in concrete
explain: Construction joints are a common feature in roads, retaining walls, channel linings, and tunnel linings wherever concreting must be carried out in separate stages.

q: 37. A concrete having slump of 6.5 cm, is said to be
explain: A slump value of 6.5 cm (65 mm) falls within the medium-to-high workability range, classifying the concrete as a plastic mix.

q: 38. Concrete is unsuitable for compaction by vibrator if it is
explain: A plastic (high-slump, wet) mix is prone to segregation and over-vibration effects when compacted with a vibrator, making it unsuitable for mechanical vibration.

q: 39. The process of mixing, transporting, placing and compacting concrete using OPC should not take more than.
explain: As per good practice referenced in this text, the complete process from mixing to compacting concrete made with OPC should be finished within 40 minutes to avoid loss of workability due to initial setting.

q: 40. As compared to moist cured concrete, the permeability of steam cured concrete is
explain: Steam curing, due to its accelerated hydration process, tends to produce a coarser pore structure, resulting in higher permeability compared to normally moist-cured concrete.

q: 41. What is the process of smoothening the surface of newly placed concrete with a trowel called?
explain: The operation of smoothening and levelling the surface of freshly placed concrete is termed floating, carried out with a float/trowel before final finishing.

q: 42. The removal of excess air after placing concrete helps in increasing the strength of concrete by :
explain: Proper compaction that removes entrapped/excess air from freshly placed concrete has been found to increase its strength by roughly 15 to 20%.
